retro:
# PR 12832 retrospective

## What worked

Fresh verified Fable High and Astra Xhigh sessions investigated equivalent scope independently. Production-JS tests quickly established the representation changes, while distinct Qt approaches established actual display semantics: screenshot rendering and Text layout/format extraction. Chromium sender source made the entity regression concrete without accessing a browser profile. Shared coordinator evidence was labelled with producer exits rather than a blanket pass.

The synthesis rejected an incomplete diagnostic fix despite agreement on the main bug. Preserving entity tokens is not sufficient if the later b/i/u restoration treats original encoded tags as original markup. Keeping this counterexample prevented overconfident copyable advice. The stale test remained a compact test-only note rather than a fabricated image regression. Lower-value capability/design comments stayed local.

## Friction and improvements

Fable's first transparent screenshot could not establish visual behavior; a white background and explicit text color fixed it. Astra's initial direct Qt-private parser approach failed at CMake configuration and then linking because the parser symbol is not exported. Using a real Text object with matching private layout headers was successful. These are preserved fixture-development failures, not PR defects or confirmed review.py bugs.

For future Qt cases, start with an offscreen Text element, assert actual parsed text and formats, and retain screenshots only when useful. When a test exits at an obsolete exact-output assertion, a labelled disposable copy can determine whether remaining tests pass without altering the source pin. Large copied Node binaries are safe and hashed but duplicate evidence storage; future tool adapters could improve efficiency, not a requirement for this PR.

No Omadev sessions were used and no Omadev issue was observed. No desktop slot or input capture was needed. Runtime isolation was maintained rather than exposing host sockets.

## Cleanup and carry-forward

All review subprocesses completed and ephemeral sandbox runtimes were torn down; reviewers report no owned survivors. Source and evidence remain preserved. No host configuration/service/package/hardware/account/audio/browser mutation, upstream posting or page opening occurred. Native session identities and historical reviewer identities are recorded. The outer assistant owns posting after a fresh upstream check and complete receipt verification.

Carry forward the process lessons only, not these PR conclusions, into the next fresh-session review.
comment: One notification-text regression was reproduced at `6f64c7941d1a24ffba692e419989aad9c508a35e`: already-escaped body text is double-escaped. ### Preserve character references from markup-aware senders In [`escapeMarkup()`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/6f64c7941d1a24ffba692e419989aad9c508a35e/shell/plugins/notifications/NotificationLogic.js#L90-L95), replacing every `&` adds another escaping layer. Actual Qt 6.11.2 `Text.StyledText` results with synthetic notification bodies: | Body supplied | Baseline displays | PR displays | |---|---|---| | `AT&T invoice` | `AT&T invoice` | `AT&T invoice` | | `Alice <alice@example.com>` | `Alice ` | `Alice <alice@example.com>` | | `AT&T` (raw control) | `AT` | `AT&T` | **Impact:** applications that escape text for the advertised `body-markup` capability now show entity spellings instead of the intended punctuation. [Chromium's notification sender](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/72b6233d6c7c2cc0012a865432fbefa079f6c244/chrome/browser/notifications/notification_platform_bridge_linux.cc#L926-L929) explicitly performs this escaping when that capability is present. Its sender behavior was source-inspected, not tested through a running browser. **Suggested change:** preserve valid character references while escaping unsupported raw tags and bare ampersands. Keep original entity tokens distinct from original b/i/u tags: merely exempting `<` from ampersand escaping lets the final restoration regex turn originally literal `<b>` into live formatting. Include that literal-tag case alongside the escaped and raw ampersand controls when validating the correction. **Verified:** the author's payload loses its red font and anchor styling; the allowed bold text remains bold. Basic b/i/u formatting, line breaks and Chromium-origin removal are retained in the exercised cases. The raw `AT&T` control above improves. **Test-only mismatch:** `test/shell.d/notifications-test.sh:122-126` passes on baseline but stops on head because the image-splice assertion still expects ``. The new escaped output contains no parsed image in the Qt test. Update that expectation and its explanation to the escaping behavior; this failure is not an image-sanitization regression. --- ## Review information **Test scope:** pinned baseline/head production JavaScript, existing notification tests, and offscreen Qt 6.11.2 Text rendering/layout with synthetic inputs. No full-shell delivery, live-browser notification or comprehensive image-fetch audit. A complete correction was not validated. **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review. **Automated AI review:** Astra initial inspection, independent Fable 5.1 and separate Astra reviews, followed by verification of claims against targeted execution, rendering and source evidence.
